# 1- The Message model defines the basic structure for messages, including content, role, parameters, and timestamps.

class Message(BaseModel):
    chat_id: Optional[str] = None  
    doc_id: Optional[str] = None
    last_login_time: Optional[datetime.datetime] = datetime.now()
    title: Optional[str] = ""
    body: Optional[str] = "" 
    user_id: Optional[str] = ""
    improved: bool = False

# 2- The Chat model represents a conversation involving multiple chats and messages on a project level.

class Chat(BaseModel, base=ChatBase):
    # Each chat belongs to exactly one project
    project_id: Optional[str] = None  
    user_id: Optional[str] = None  
    doc_id: Optional[str] = ""         # Common across allkanban columns linked with this conversation
    
    # Properties unique to the project (doc_id and project_id)
    doc_owner: Optional[str] = ""  
    doc_type: Optional[str] = "".split("/")[-1]
    
    @classmethod
    def _get chats(cls) -> List[Chat]:
        chat_info = cls projecting to get all chats in a project from the API
        return list(chat_info['doc_id'])

# 3- The Kanban class represents individual kanban messages or columns within the context of a chat.

class KanbanCol(BaseModel, base=Message):
    pass

# 4- The Column model defines the basic schema for the column interface, including doc_id and all other properties,
# which are shared across allkanban columns linked with this column in a project instance.

class Column(BaseModel):
